brief: Jackie Leven in seiner Doll-by-Doll-Zeit: drei raue, deutlich abstrahierte Entwürfe. Gesichtszüge wiedererkennbar; neue Bildkomposition ohne fotografische Szenerie. Keine Aussage über eine urheberrechtliche Freigabe.

variants.title: Rauer Siebdruck
variants.initial_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a single striking illustration for a Jackie Leven tribute website, portraying his young rebellious Doll by Doll period.
Reference images: BOTH supplied photos are FACIAL IDENTITY references only. Study the specific young man's proportions, eyes and eyelids, nose, mouth, cheek and jaw structure, forehead and swept-back dark hair with longer neck-length strands. Preserve those recognizable traits and his youthful clean-shaven appearance. Do not age him, beautify him, sharpen his jaw, caricature him, or turn him into a generic punk singer.
Create an independently conceived portrait, NOT a stylized reproduction, tracing, crop or filter of either photograph. Invent a new composition, light, head angle and body arrangement. No photographic background, ladder, brickwork, companions, or copied shirt pattern.
New composition shared across this set: vertical 4:5, mid-chest-up portrait with an asymmetrical shoulder line, torso turned toward the viewer's left, head turned slightly back toward the viewer's right in a gentle three-quarter view, chin subtly lifted, eyes looking just past the viewer. Strong directional light creates a newly designed graphic shadow on one side of the face. Keep the full hair silhouette within the frame and enough paper margin. A simple dark open-neck shirt merges into abstract lower shapes. The attitude is uncompromising, alert and restless, with a closed relaxed mouth, not a theatrical scowl. Rebel energy comes from posture, contrast and material.
Abstraction must be in the mark-making, tonal shapes, clothing and setting, NOT in distorted facial anatomy. Preserve exact recognizable feature spacing and contours within the simplification.
No text, lettering, logos, symbols, signatures, borders, instruments, accessories, extra people, props or watermarks. No copper engraving, antique effect, sepia, fine crosshatching, polished glamour or photographic gradients.
Style/medium: bold handmade two-ink screenprint with raw underground rock-poster energy. Ink black and vermilion red on clean chalk-white paper. Reduce the portrait to a small number of large, decisive, flat shapes; use paper white as the facial highlight, black for the main shadows and hair. Retain the specific eyes, nose and mouth through carefully cut negative-space edges. The face is drawn and designed, never a thresholded photograph. Slightly broken edges and selective dry ink dropout, but broad untextured areas keep it graphic and readable at website thumbnail scale.
Composition accents: a single off-center block of red behind the head and a restrained red overprint extending into the shoulder area, with irregular edges. Black hair and shirt form a forceful silhouette. Strong empty white space balances the mass. No full-frame decorative grunge, halftone photograph, microscopic detail or many tonal steps. The result should feel immediate, angular in its graphic arrangement but anatomically faithful, contemporary and unapologetic.
variants.revision_prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, an existing newly composed portrait illustration. Images 2 and 3 are supporting facial-identity references ONLY, showing the same young Jackie Leven.
Make one targeted artistic correction to image 1: radically simplify the rendering of the face, neck, hair and shirt into unmistakably hand-designed abstract marks and large tonal shapes. The current face is much too photographic and finely textured.
PRESERVE the existing independently composed head angle, shoulder placement, crop, young age, expression and actual facial anatomy and likeness. Do not revert to the poses or backgrounds of the reference photos. Maintain the exact eye positions and shapes, nose profile, lip shape, jaw and forehead of this individual. Abstraction reduces marks and tones without stretching, beautifying, caricaturing or distorting his face.
Remove ALL photographic grain, soft grayscale shading, skin pores, fine stippling and thin individual hair detail from the face and hair. Do NOT merely increase contrast on a photo. Invent intentional drawn boundaries of a small number of broad light and dark shapes. The shapes should be large and visibly flat even when seen at full resolution. Exposed light paper makes most of the forehead and lit cheek. Eyes, nose and mouth need a few precise economical marks; shadow under the jaw is a single graphic shape. Let edges remain open where possible.
Preserve the palette and overall arrangement of the target, with stronger graphic economy and uncompromising rock-art energy. A single vertical 4:5 image. No text, letters, symbols, additional objects, watermark or frame.
Medium: strongly reduced TWO-COLOR handmade screenprint, pure black and vermilion on white. The face should read as a carefully hand-cut stencil of around 6–9 broad shapes with a few precise feature details, clearly recognizable but radically simplified. Flat contiguous black shadows with sharp deliberate cut contours, zero gray, zero halftone or skin grain, no photostat look. Preserve the red background block and red shoulder overprint. Keep rough ink dropout only sparingly at the exterior edges of the shirt and color block. No comic-book style outlines or thick cartoon features.

Clear tension, rough material edges, confident large areas of color, no ornamental decoration, no newspaper text, no type, no nostalgia or sepia. The result should have the visual force and economy of an independently designed experimental rock record sleeve.
